responses: I reviewed `feat/quote-pdf` (commit cda58ff, which adds `app/pdf.py` and `tests/test_pdf.py`) against ADR-0007, then did a security pass. **Verdict: don't merge yet.** There's one gap against the ADR and one security issue that gets worse once real PDF rendering is added. I didn't change any code. I also couldn't run the tests, because shell access was denied in this session; please run `python -m pytest -q` yourself before merging. ## ADR-0007 compliance | ADR requirement | Status | Evidence | |---|---|---| | Page size A4 | ✅ Met | `app/pdf.py:6`, tested | | `dir="rtl"` for Arabic quotes | ✅ Met | `app/pdf.py:11`, tested for both RTL and LTR | | Rendered with WeasyPrint | ⚠️ Not done yet | Rendering is a stub. `route_quote_pdf` returns HTML, not a PDF, even though it's documented as `GET /quotes/{id}/pdf`. WeasyPrint isn't declared as a dependency anywhere. | | Built from HTML templates | ⚠️ Partly | The commit says "template", but the HTML is built from an inline f-string (`app/pdf.py:12-14`). There's no template file. | | Fonts embedded, never taken from the system | ❌ Missing | There's no `@font-face` rule and no `app/fonts/` directory. Arabic text would fall back to system fonts, which is exactly what the ADR forbids. | If the stub is meant to be a deliberate first step, say so in the PR and track the WeasyPrint and font work. Otherwise the branch doesn't yet deliver what ADR-0007 decided. ## Security 1. **HTML injection, which turns into local file read or server-side requests once WeasyPrint is added (High).** `q.customer` and `ln.sku` go into the HTML unescaped (`app/pdf.py:12-13`). WeasyPrint downloads the resources referenced in the HTML, so an injected customer name containing ``, `` or `` could read local files or reach internal services, and attachments get embedded in the PDF. Even without WeasyPrint, if this HTML is ever served to a browser it's stored XSS. - **Fix:** escape every value (`html.escape`, or Jinja2 with autoescaping), and give WeasyPrint a custom `url_fetcher` that only allows files from `app/fonts/`. 2. **No authorization check on the route (Medium, needs your confirmation).** Anyone who can call it can fetch any quote by changing `quote_id`. That's fine only if a layer outside this module checks that the caller may see that quote. I couldn't find such a layer in the repo. 3. **Secrets:** none in the diff, and `.env` is gitignored. ✅ ## Correctness issues found along the way - An unknown `quote_id` raises `KeyError` (`app/quotes.py:33`), which would surface as a 500 error instead of a 404. - The language check only matches exactly `"ar"`, so `"ar-EG"` or `"AR"` would render left-to-right. The HTML also has no `lang` attribute or ``, which matters for Arabic text shaping. - There are no tests for escaping, fonts, or unknown IDs. **Before merging I'd want:** values escaped, a restricted `url_fetcher` (or a note to add one with WeasyPrint), embedded fonts or an explicit follow-up for them, and an answer on where authorization happens.
